surfaces.part: shaft with number 1 panel and gray lower panel

answer.evidence: The head (rows 0-9) widens 10, 12, 14 at the top and then ends flat at row 9 directly above the narrower shaft. It is a chamfered, hat-like top, so the width profile never narrows again and there is no ellipse. The white face has a small icon on rows 3-5 and a gray bevel band on rows 6-8. It reads as a front-facing sign box, not a horizontal plate seen from above. Row 10 is a gap and the shaft below (rows 11-29, width 10) is a vertical face with a teal header, a yellow '1' panel and a gray lower panel. None of these has an edge line or eave shadow that would mark a top surface, so the object is a front elevation with at most a 1-2 row rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small standing sign post with a pale cap, a dark-teal body and a yellow '1' plate. It has 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 6 for bus-shelter-a, 12 for kiosk-a and 20 for vending-a. That puts it above the bus shelter, level with the kiosk and below the vending machine. Near-flat coverage is 9%, the same as the bus shelter and low. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (dark blue-teal beside the body), not black. Shading is about 4 steps on the body and cap, with highlight edges and a shadowed side, a little shallower than the kiosk but comparable for a thin sign prop. The sign face and cap show some grain and a bevel, not flat fills. A careful artist would accept it next to the shipped modern_city references without it looking thinner or more sticker-like.
